Name: Aegaeon
Description: god of violent sea storms and ally of the Titans

Name: Achelous
Description: shark-shaped sea spirit

Name: Amphitrite
Description: sea goddess and consort of Poseidon

Name: Benthesikyme
Description: daughter of Poseidon, who resided in Ethiopia

Name: Brizo
Description: patron goddess of sailors, who sent prophetic dreams

Name: Ceto
Description: goddess of the dangers of the ocean and of sea monsters

Name: Charybdis
Description: a sea monster and spirit of whirlpools and the tide

Name: Cymopoleia
Description: a daughter of Poseidon married to the Giant Briareus

Name: Delphin
Description: the leader of the dolphins, Poseidon placed him in the sky as the constellation Delphin

Name: Eidothea
Description: prophetic sea nymph and daughter of Proteus

Name: Glaucus
Description: the fisherman's sea god

Name: Gorgons
Description: three monstrous sea spirits

Name: Medusa
Description: the only mortal of the three

Name: Graeae
Description: three ancient sea spirits who personified the white foam of the sea; they shared one eye and one tooth between them

Name: Harpies
Description: winged spirits of sudden, sharp gusts of wind

Name: Hippocampi
Description: horses of the sea that have the upper-body of a horse and the lower-body of a fish

Name: Ichthyocentaurs
Description: a race of centaurine sea-gods with the upper bodies of men, the lower fore-parts of horses, ending in the serpentine tails of fish

Name: Karkinos
Description: a giant crab who allied itself with the Hydra against Heracles. When it died, Hera placed it in the sky as the constellation Cancer

Name: Ladon
Description: a hundred-headed sea serpent who guarded the western reaches of the sea, and the island and golden apples of the Hesperides

Name: Leucothea
Description: a sea goddess who aided sailors in distress

Name: Nereides
Description: sea nymphs

Name: Thetis
Description: leader of the Nereids who presided over the spawning of marine life in the sea

Name: Arethusa
Description: a daughter of Nereus who was transformed into a fountain

Name: Galene
Description: goddess of calm seas

Name: Psamathe
Description: goddess of sand beaches

Name: Nereus
Description: the old man of the sea, and the god of the sea's rich bounty of fish

Name: Nerites
Description: a sea spirit who was transformed into a shell-fish by Aphrodite

Name: Oceanus
Description: Titan god of the Earth-encircling river Oceanus, the font of all the Earth's fresh-water

Name: Palaemon
Description: a young sea god who aided sailors in distress

Name: Phorcys
Description: god of the hidden dangers of the deep

Name: Pontos
Description: primeval god of the sea, father of the fish and other sea creatures

Name: Proteus
Description: a shape-shifting, prophetic old sea god, and the herdsman of Poseidon's seals

Name: Poseidon
Description: king of the sea and lord of the sea gods; also god of rivers, flood and drought, earthquakes, and horses

Name: Scylla
Description: monstrous sea goddess

Name: Sirens
Description: sea nymphs who lured sailors to their death with their song

Name: Telchines
Description: sea spirits native to the island of Rhodes; the gods killed them when they turned to evil magic

Name: Dexithea
Description: mother of Euxanthios by Minos

Name: Tethys
Description: Titan goddess of the sources fresh water, and the mother of the rivers, springs, streams, fountains, and clouds

Name: Thalassa
Description: primeval goddess of the sea and consort of Pontos

Name: Thaumas
Description: god of the wonders of the sea

Name: Thoosa
Description: goddess of swift currents

Name: Triteia
Description: daughter of Triton and companion of Ares

Name: Triton
Description: fish-tailed son and herald of Poseidon

Name: Tritones
Description: fish-tailed spirits in Poseidon's retinue
